BACKGROUND

Each month, the San Marino Police Department provides a brief and informational update
on crime, traffic issues, and other items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety
Commission.

DISCUSSION

911 Remembrance 2025
On September 11, sworn SMPD personnel honored the
memory of those who served, volunteered, and lost
their lives on this solemn day. In partnership with SMFD,
a memorial flag ceremony was held to pay tribute to the
victims and heroes of the September 11 attacks. This
observance reflects our continued commitment to
remembering the lives lost, the courage of the first
responders and survivors, and the unity and resilience
that emerged in the aftermath.

DETECTIVE BUREAU INVESTIGATIONS

For the month of September, the San Marino Police Department Detective Bureau
completed the following activities and caseload.

Theft From a Motor Vehicle -Update on August 2025 Investigation
Officers responded to a radio call involving theft from a motor vehicle in the 1100 Block
of Lorain Road. The victim’s unlocked vehicle was parked on the street in front of their
residence. Several items were stolen from the victim’s vehicle including cash,
identification, and credit and debit cards. While conducting their investigation the
officers located evidence: a key fob that was left inside the vehicle that did not belong
to the victim. The key fob led investigators to the suspect.

  PAGE 6 of 46
 After reporting the grand theft, fraudulent charges were made on the victim’s account at
Costco in Alhambra. On September 10, 2025, Detectives conducted a follow up
investigation at Costco and were able to locate the suspect’s vehicle and information
regarding the identity of the suspect. The detectives’ investigation revealed that the
suspect is wanted in multiple jurisdictions, has an extensive criminal record, and is
currently on probation for carjacking.

Monday, September 29, 2025, detectives were notified that the involved suspect was
scheduled to appear for a probation violation hearing at Van Nuys Court. San Marino
Police Department detectives located the suspect at Van Nuys Court and took him into
custody for PC 487, Grand Theft, PC 496, Receiving Stolen Property, and PC 530.5(2),
Identity Theft with Prior Convictions. The suspect, Arutyun Baltayan (D.O.B. 07/20/79,
Sylmar) was transported to Pasadena City Jail for booking. This felony case was filed
with the Los Angeles District Attorney’s Office (DA) and detectives are scheduled to
appear in court on this case in October 2025.

Theft from a Motor Vehicle - 1400 Block of San Marino Avenue
Friday, September 5, 2025, officers were dispatched to a commercial business regarding
the theft of approximately $8K in tools taken from work vans parked at the business.
Employees of the business observed the suspect’s vehicle and described it as a white
Mercedes Benz sedan. The suspect’s vehicle in this case (white Mercedez Benz sedan) is
linked to the following theft from vehicle that took place on September 25, in the 2200
Block of Lorain Road.

Theft from a Motor Vehicle - 2200 Block of Lorain Road
Thursday, September 25, 2025, officers were flagged down by two male subjects
standing next to a pick-up truck. The subjects reported that they had just confronted an
unknown suspect inside their vehicle attempting to steal their construction equipment.
The victim video recorded the confrontation. San Marino Police Detectives contacted
the San Bernadino Sheriff’s Intelligence Unit. Investigators obtained the victim’s video
footage of the confrontation with and were able to identify the suspect captured in the
footage. This case is ongoing.

Detective Bureau personnel in collaboration with the El Segundo Police Department,
Redondo Beach Police Department, and the San Bernardino Police Department are
reviewing multiple cases involving a driver of a white Mercedes Benz possibly linked to
additional vehicle burglaries in our city and elsewhere.

Residential Burglary – Update on December 2024 Investigation
In December 2024, officers were dispatched to the 1100 Block of Lorain Road for an
audible alarm. The officers discovered a broken window that allowed access to the
residence. Officers and detectives at scene recovered latent fingerprints and cigarette
  PAGE 7 of 46
 butts left behind by the suspect. The recovered evidence was submitted to the Los
Angeles County Sheriff’s Laboratory for analysis. Detective Bureau received notification
from the lab indicating a positive match to a known suspect SMPD officers arrested in
January 2025, in a separate incident in our city. This case has been forwarded to the DA
to obtain an arrest warrant for PC 459, Burglary, for the suspect. The investigation is
ongoing.

Great investigative work by our Detective Bureau.

investigation and filed the following charges against the suspect: PC 211, Robbery, PC

TRAFFIC

Traffic Enforcement
During the month of September, officers conducted a total of 297 traffic enforcement
stops as part of ongoing efforts to promote road safety and compliance with traffic laws.
Of these stops, 103 resulted in citations being issued, highlighting the continued need
for active enforcement to deter violations and encourage responsible driving behavior.
These enforcement activities serve as a reminder of the importance of adhering to traffic
regulations to ensure the safety of all.

Additionally, personnel conducted e-bike safety presentations throughout the school
district. Officers shared information about new e-bike classifications. SMPD is actively
collaborating with city staff to develop a new city ordinance regarding e-bikes, aimed
not only at promoting safety but also at educating youth in the community.

TECHNOLOGY

The Police Department has utilized AXON (a.k.a. TASER) devices as a means of less lethal
technology for over 20 years. For many years, the X26 Model was the “gold standard,”
adopted by numerous law enforcement agencies across the United States. In 2023,
AXON released the TASER 10, which can achieve effective connections at a greater
range, creating more time to de-escalate a situation. Additionally, the TASER 10 can
deploy up to 10 individually targeted probes without reloading. The Police Department
will be transitioning from the outdated X26 Model to the new and improved TASER 10.
The TASER 10’s should be received by the end of the year, and department-wide
training will follow shortly thereafter.

The new Motorola mobile in-car radios are expected to be installed in all patrol vehicles
by the end of the year. This is a huge advancement in technology for our field
personnel, increasing communication reliability and officer safety.

Currently, the Police Department has a total of seven police officer vacancies, one of
which is a position frozen for the 2025-26 Fiscal Year. The past three vacancies are a
result of staff who have recently retired. Our recruiting team continues to pursue
interested police officer applicants to fill the vacancies.

We are currently processing one lateral police officer candidate, who is currently in the
background portion of the process. There are multiple police officer recruit candidates
that are at various stages of the process. Two police officer recruit candidates recently
began backgrounds. If successful, they will move on to a Chief’s Interview and could
potentially begin a police academy class in the first quarter of 2026.

The written and physical examinations will be administered on a continuous basis, until
the remaining positions are filled.

A MOMENT IN TIME

In September 1967, the FBI launched the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a
significant advancement in law enforcement technology. The NCIC provides real-time
access to crime data across jurisdictions, transforming how agencies share information
on stolen property, missing persons, and criminal records. This innovation marked a
critical milestone in modern policing and continues to support public safety efforts
nationwide.

DISCUSSION

Ready San Marino: An Informational Town Hall on Infrastructure and
Earthquake Preparedness
In preparation for the annual Great ShakeOut drill on October 16, the San
Marino Fire Department hosted a Town Hall on October 15 focused on
earthquake preparedness and the potential impacts of a major earthquake on
the City of San Marino. Dr. Lucy Jones, a renowned seismologist and creator
of the Great ShakeOut drill and California’s earthquake advisory system,
joined the Department to provide an educational overview of earthquake
causes, their effects, and the history of seismic activity in Southern California.
Dr. Jones shared valuable insights on how residents can better prepare for
future events. Representatives from Southern California Edison and California
American Water Company also attended to answer residents’ questions about
how utility services may be affected following a disaster.

  PAGE 24 of 46
 When asked how residents prepare their homes for earthquakes, Dr. Jones
said “bolting your house to the foundation is the single most important thing
you can do.” The State of California offers Earthquake Brace + Bolt, an annual
retrofit grant program to assist homeowners with this process and provides
financial assistance and a list of qualified contractors. Applications open
annually in the month of September.

2025 California Fire Code
On Friday, September 26, the San Marino City Council adopted the 2025
Edition of the California Building and Standards Code and California Fire Code.
The 2025 Fire Code included new provisions to bolster wildfire preparedness
in the City’s Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. The provisions address
vents, open eaves, and enclosed eaves and are designed to prevent wind-
driven embers, the leading cause of home ignitions during wildfires, from
entering or accumulating in vulnerable parts of buildings. These updates not
only align San Marino with State best practices, but also strengthen
community resilience against wildfire threats. The new provisions will apply to
new construction, additions, and remodels within San Marino’s designated
hazard zone.

Personnel
On Monday, September 15 and Tuesday, September 16, the San Marino,
South Pasadena, and San Gabriel Fire Departments conducted a joint Battalion
Chief promotional examination. The examination aimed to fill one shared
Division Chief vacancy for the San Marino and South Pasadena Fire
Departments, and one Battalion Chief position with the San Gabriel Fire
Department. Over the two-day exam, candidates participated in a written
exercise, oral interview, a formal presentation, and a simulated incident
command exercise. The examination resulted in three successful candidates
for the San Marino / South Pasadena shared Division Chief position. South
Pasadena Fire Captain Dan Dunn achieved the highest score and was
promoted to the position of Division Chief on October 6, 2025. The remaining
successful candidates will be placed on a consideration list for future
promotional opportunities.

The Fire Department is currently conducting interviews for the position of
Firefighter/Paramedic. The application period closed on September 30, after
receiving a total of 17 applications. There is currently one vacancy at the
Firefighter/Paramedic rank. Additionally, there is one vacancy at the Captain
position due to a long term, duty connected injury that is being filled by acting
personnel; that Captain recently announced his retirement, effective
December 2025. A total of ten candidates were invited for interviews, a ride
along, and a paramedic assessment evaluation. The top three candidates
selected have begun a criminal background investigation process.

  NEW FIRE CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS

The City of San Marino has adopted specific fire and ignition resistant construction standards from the State
of California’s Wildland-Urban Interface Code (WUI). The new standards go into effect January 1, 2026.

The City of San Marino is not located in any of the State-designated Fire Hazard Severity Zones (FHSZ); the
City is located in a Local Responsibility Area (LRA). These new standards will help protect properties located
within the City’s designated Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone (VHFHSZ).

Currently, properties located in the City’s designated VHFHSZ must comply with previously adopted
vegetation management provisions of the San Marino Municipal Code; the new fire construction standards
will only be enforced on these parcels. The new standards will only apply to new structures, additions to
existing structures, and remodeling affecting the roof eaves and ventilation opening on the exterior of the
structure.

  What’s Changing?
Vents
  • Why: Vents are a common entry point for embers during wildfires.
  • New Standard: Structures must use ember-resistant vents or, based on the location of the vent on
  the structure, the vents may be of non-corrosive, noncombustible materials with openings not
  exceeding 1/8 of an inch.
  • Benefit: Reduces the chance of embers entering attics and crawlspaces.

Open Eaves
  • Why: Open eaves can trap embers and allow fire to spread.
  • New Standard: It provides builders several prescriptive options to increase the fire resistivity of the
  open eave while maintaining the desirable architectural style.
  • Benefit: Prevents embers from igniting combustible materials and entering the structures at the
  eave.

Enclosed Eaves
  • Why: Even enclosed eaves when constructed of combustible materials may be overcome by the
  embers and spread the fire.
  • New Standard: The enclosed eaves finish materials must be non combustible, ignition resistant or
  fire treated lumber; it also allows the designer to retain the desirable architectural style.
  • Benefit: Stops embers from being trapped by exposed rafters and reduces the chances of
  smoldering and ignition.

  Why This Matters
  ✓  Strengthens fire safety for residents
  ✓  Aligns San Marino with California best practices
  ✓  Helps protect homes and neighborhoods in our most vulnerable areas

  The new standard is located in Section 12.03.09 of the San Marino Municipal Code
